messages.author: 1d74b0364284e0de
messages.subject: Data binning to infinity
parts:
Hi,

Regarding binned data, I understand that for a 0-50 meter distance bin the observation should be listed at 25 m, a 50-100 meter bin data should be listed as 75 m, etc. But for an outer bin that includes all observations past a certain distance, such as all observations over 50 meters, how should those observations be listed?

Thanks!

messages.author: 39f0839e8d6a4470
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Data binning to infinity
parts:
Hi Alex,

For binned data you need start and end points for each bin. These must be defined in the data filter for binned data. (The bin options in the model definition are purely for diagnostic purposes). The values of the datapoints within the bin is not important as it is actually anasyed in bins but usually people do use the mid point as you have suggested.

Your last bin is going to be problematic. Usually a bin with no end point would be excluded from the analyses, there is no way to specify an infinite end point (doing this would result in a bin of 0 height any way). Survey protocol may include one on the record sheet so that observers don't feel the need to heap observations just beyond a truncation distance into the final bin (which would cause analysis issues) but this bin would not be used for the analyses. 

Laura
 
Dr. L. Marshall
Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling
University of St. Andrews
